item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Festive events announced for True’s Yard Fisherfolk Museum
True’s Yard Fisherfolk Museum in King’s Lynn is hosting a series of Christmas events following a grant of over £2,500. The ‘Reel Bright Idea’ project includes a free Dickensian trail launching in November, alongside an exhibition on the history of Christmas tree decorations.
Families can also enjoy free yoga classes, craft sessions, and a Christmas fair. Other highlights include a carol concert at All Saints’ Church on December 9 and evening museum openings in mid-December. Many activities are free, though some require advance booking. For full details on the schedule or to reserve a place, visit the True’s Yard website, call 01553 770479, or email info@truesyard.co.uk.

item.title: Future of Queen Elizabeth Hospital services to be discussed
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Future of Queen Elizabeth Hospital services to be discussed
The Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group Board is meeting on Monday, November 2, to discuss a new clinical strategy for the region. The board will review a "Case for Change" document, which examines how healthcare services might develop over the coming decades.
This follows public concern regarding reports that accident and emergency, intensive care, and maternity services at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn could face closure. However, the hospital group has stressed that no decisions have been made. They state the meeting is not a consultation on service changes, but rather the start of a conversation about how to improve care while addressing staffing pressures and changing population needs.

item.title: Heacham man fined for cannabis possession in King’s Lynn
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Heacham man fined for cannabis possession in King’s Lynn
A 46-year-old man from Heacham has been fined after being caught with cannabis in King’s Lynn town centre. Samuel Wright, of Station Road, was arrested on the evening of October 4 following reports regarding his behaviour on Littleport Street. Police officers searched Mr Wright and discovered 16 grams of the Class B drug in his pocket.
Appearing at Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, Mr Wright entered a guilty plea. The court heard that the defendant, who works as a grounds worker, had not committed an offence in the last five years. He was ordered to pay a total of £1,093, which includes a £720 fine, a £288 victim surcharge, and £85 in court costs.

item.title: Wisbech cinema to host screening of new British documentary
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Wisbech cinema to host screening of new British documentary
A new British feature documentary, The Fastest Bicycle, is coming to The Light Cinema in Wisbech next month. Directed by double BAFTA-winner Michael B. Clifford, the film follows a London-based team attempting to compete in the World Human Powered Speed Challenge in Nevada. The documentary chronicles the group's seven-year journey, detailing the various technical and personal challenges they faced while preparing for the event.
The screening is scheduled for Thursday, November 12, at 7.30 pm. The film is dedicated to the late designer Mike Burrows and explores themes of perseverance and community within the world of high-speed cycling. Tickets are available for the local showing as part of a nationwide release.

item.title: King’s Lynn concert celebrates cultural diversity through music and dance
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn concert celebrates cultural diversity through music and dance
A sold-out concert at the King’s Lynn Masonic Centre on Sunday, October 25, showcased a blend of Indian classical and Western artistic traditions. Organised by Sursarang Arts, the "Music Beyond Borders" event featured performances ranging from Kathak and Flamenco dancing to violin and vocal collaborations. The Mayor of King’s Lynn and West Norfolk, Councillor Steve Bearshaw, was among the capacity audience.
Directors Dr Prabir Mitra and Sanjukta Mitra hosted the evening to highlight how the arts can bridge different cultures. The programme included an instrumental duet by visiting artist Pandit Pallab Bandyopadhyay and concluded with a grand finale involving all performers. The organisers hope the event will foster greater cultural appreciation across the region.

Search underway for unclaimed £1M Lotto prize in Fenland
A search is underway for a National Lottery player in Fenland who has won £1 million but has yet to come forward. The winning ticket was purchased for the draw held on Saturday, October 17. The successful numbers were 4, 9, 15, 32, 38, 42, with 2 as the Bonus Ball.
Lottery operator Allwyn is urging residents to check their tickets, including those kept in cars or kitchen drawers. The winner has until midnight on April 15, 2027, to claim the prize. Anyone who believes they have the winning ticket should contact the National Lottery line on 0333 2345050 or email help@national-lottery.co.uk. If the prize remains unclaimed, the money will be donated to National Lottery-funded projects.

item.title: Wisbech students win national award for hedgehog conservation business
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Wisbech students win national award for hedgehog conservation business
Three construction students from the College of West Anglia in Wisbech have achieved national success in the Peter Jones Foundation’s Tycoon Enterprise Competition. Finn McAuley, Marc Watson, and Erikas Rimkus, known as The Fabulous Baker’s Trio, secured joint first place in the Business for Good category. The students were recognised for their project, which involves building hedgehog houses to provide shelter for local wildlife. The enterprise also supported the charity Ryston Rachel’s Hedgehog Hotel through fundraising efforts. College staff praised the trio for their hard work and dedication, noting that the project successfully combined practical construction skills with a commitment to environmental conservation.
